title: Story Tea
content: Let professional storyteller Pyn Stockman guide you on an extraordinary storytelling journey from the comfort of the library. Pyn will wrap you up in beautiful tales crafted from British myth, legend and folklore, whilst you brew your own ‘story tea’ in fine china teapots guided by master herbalist, Arlene Burnett. These tales are magical, mesmerising and often have a dark twist – making it a perfect story mix. You’ll find elements from the stories shared this evening may make their way into your own unique story tea which you can sip and enjoy while sitting back and relaxing along with this masterful performance.

title: Stoke Book Club: Book Chat
content: No book festival is complete without launching a new book club. Join the Stoke Book Festival’s Book Club and begin your journey into books.

title: Music & Words: An Evening of English Song
content: Enjoy a stunning performance by the City of Stoke-on-Trent Symphony Orchestra and vocalist Jordan Harding. They will take you on a musical journey through English song and stories linked to famous authors, poets, and composers, including some new discoveries. The concert begins at 7 pm, but arrive by 6:15pm for a pre-concert talk with Artistic Director Joe Hearson, who will introduce the evening and discuss the music's inspiration from poems and words.

title: A Creative Evening with Soke-on-Trent’s Poet Laureate, Steven Beattie
content: Join us for an evening of poetry with Stoke-on-Trent’s Poet Laureate, Steven Beattie. Steven will be talking about how he came to be awarded the Poet laureate title, his love of poetry as well as sharing some of his superb poetry. Steven will also be sharing some poetry prompts and encouraging the audience to put pen to paper. The perfect evening for poetry lovers and budding poets alike. This is an adult event and will contain adult themes and language.

title: Take 10 to Read
content: Each year on 10 October for World Mental Health Day the National Literacy Trust call on the nation to #Take10ToRead. Join us on the festival Saturday with your favourite book (or a new one) and join us at one of our venues, Stoke Minster or Stoke Library for free Event refreshment a moment of peace and tranquillity inside or outside and take 10 to read.

title: Letters to My Future Self
content: Join Kate Leake, an author, illustrator and Stoke-on-Trent’s current Creativity Laureate. Kate will host an interactive, creative ‘Letters to My Future Self’ workshop at Stoke Market as part of the inaugural Stoke Book Festival. Participants can choose to write a letter, a poem, a short piece of prose or even draw a picture dedicated to themselves. When you’ve completed your letter, hand it in and the festival will post these letters to you a year later.Letters to My Future Self is a chance to reflect on the past or envision the future – with creative tips and guidance from Kate as you illustrate your message, hopefully bringing a smile to your future self.

title: Local Author networking and Publishing Panel
content: Are you an author or writer based in North Staffordshire? The Stoke Book Festival is hosting a mixer event where you can meet fellow local writers, receive advice and tips from publishers and published authors. Join us for refreshments and conversation to support your writing journey.
